NO are soft against the run (132 yds/game allowed), and LV feed Ashton Jeanty a heavy 61% carry share — a rushing-yards spot.

The NO host the LV as favorites of 3.0, with the total set at 42.5 — a market that implies a NO 23–20 scoreline. Running the game forward from that baseline, we expect a contest that spends roughly 31% of its snaps with NO in front, 41% within one score, and 27% with NO chasing. That distribution is the engine of everything below: game state is what turns a team's tendencies into a specific player's workload, so before we get to individuals it's worth being explicit about how this game is likely to be played.

This is a coin-flip script. With only 3.0 points separating them, neither team projects to spend much time in a blowout state — most of the game lives in the 'close' bucket, where play-calling stays balanced and usage tracks each player's established role rather than being distorted by score. In tight games the stars on both sides see their normal, dependable workloads, and there is less garbage-time leakage to backups.

The Key Matchups

Tre Tucker faces a tough cover — NO hold WR1s to just 51 yds/game (vs ~58); a rec-yards under lean.

Touchdown Board

Juwan Johnson is a live anytime-TD dart — LV are leaky to tight ends in the end zone (0.32 TE TDs/game vs ~0.24).

Chris Olave carries TD equity — LV surrender 0.44 WR1 receiving scores a game.

Tre Tucker carries TD equity — NO surrender 0.47 WR1 receiving scores a game.

In the red zone LV throw it (59% pass inside the 20) — Tre Tucker's TD equity over a goal-line back.

Game Script, Pace & Environment

Indoors — a dome removes weather variance and historically nudges passing efficiency up; a small tailwind for the passing games.

NO — a run-heavy offense

NO are one of the league's more run-committed offenses: on early downs while leading, they pass just 37% of the time, against a league average of 44% — a genuine clock-bleeding identity, not noise (it holds after shrinking their sample toward the league).

Travis Etienne (14 carries, 60 yards) projects to his baseline workload — no strong script push either way in a close game.

Chris Olave projects for 10 targets and 83 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, Juwan Johnson (TE, 5 targets, 40 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

LV — a balanced offense

LV are a balanced offense — their run/pass split by game state tracks the league closely (46% pass when leading vs 44% average), so their players' usage is driven more by role than by any strong situational lean.

Ashton Jeanty (18 carries, 65 yards) projects to his baseline workload — no strong script push either way in a close game.

Tre Tucker projects for 6 targets and 45 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, Brock Bowers (TE, 6 targets, 49 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

What to watch

The single biggest swing factor is availability — use the injury tool in the sidebar to mark anyone out; a starter's absence doesn't just remove his line, it redistributes his targets and carries to specific teammates, and the report and projections rebuild around it. Beyond that: if this game breaks toward the projected 3-point margin, the garbage-time backups (the ◆-flagged rows below) are where soft lines and real edge tend to appear — those depth players get fed in blowouts, and the market is slowest to price them.

This preview and the projections below regenerate through the week as injuries, weather and line moves update the inputs.
